notes: Editorial, verified milestones only. Historical entries are dated changes, not retroactively assigned software versions. Entries require matching Git commits and live internal topic routes.

releases.title: Explore why planet mass and size both affect gravity
releases.summary: The planet-weight comparison now includes a hands-on experiment: change mass and radius separately and see the gravity equation, a symbolic radius circle, and the explanation respond together. Published NASA equatorial gravity ratios were also reconciled with an explicitly labeled idealized model.
releases.students: Try four times the mass at the same radius, then twice the radius at the same mass. See why the first makes gravity four times stronger, but the second reduces it to one quarter. Compare a Jupiter-like theoretical model with the real reference value.
releases.teachers: Run a predict–change–explain activity with independent mass/radius controls, live numerical outcomes and an honest schematic. Explain that actual effective equatorial gravity differs from the simplified non-rotating GM/R² relationship, and gas giants lack solid surfaces.
releases.developers: Added a static-first native SVG radius symbol, four physical thought experiments and accessible sliders, corrected NASA effective equatorial data for giant planets in the shared fact source, kept scientific evidence links, and added independent ci/verify_gravity_mechanism.mjs to deploy and read-only Health. Verified 320/390/1280 responsive states and blocked-JavaScript fallback.

releases.title: Scale graphics now agree with the numbers
releases.summary: Planetary illustrations use accurate diameter ratios. Astronomy units, transit-candidate limits and the orbital teaching model now disclose their definitions and approximations. The image-evidence guide prioritizes authentic NASA observations.
releases.students: Compare planetary diameters on one true scale. Manipulate an illustrative transit with live relative brightness and learn why a recurring dip alone does not prove a planet.
releases.teachers: Use corrected linear/log scale labels, source-backed IAU definitions, false-positive warnings and clear model-only units during lessons.
releases.developers: Source-grounded 28-page learner-needs audit, corrected visible glyph ratios and model claims, and a new automated science-truth gate in build and health workflows.

releases.title: Examples now open when you ask to see them
releases.summary: The three image-reading examples stay closed until selected, and the planetary size comparison works with keyboard or touch. The mobile Search button remains separate from the lesson-navigation row. Moon phase and tide model presets now accurately show which mode is selected. Light-year, universe zoom and planet-size models now show readable reference values before interactive scripts finish loading.
releases.students: Select “View an example” to read one explanation; select it again to hide the text. Planet size buttons update the comparison by touch, mouse, or keyboard. Moon phase and spring/neap tide shortcuts now also reflect the selected model state. The Sun light-travel reference, first universe-scale step and Earth–Jupiter comparison remain readable during loading; controls activate only when ready. The Moon remains fully visible through every position in the tidal-locking orbit, including on narrow mobile screens.
releases.teachers: The illustration/observation/model examples now match their visible open state. Keyboard-operable planet controls and an announced fact readout support classroom accessibility. Moon phase and tide preset selection states now remain synchronized with displayed model values and assistive controls. Three interactive lessons now retain factual first-screen content even if JavaScript is unavailable, instead of starting with empty feedback. The tidally locked and hypothetical Moon marker demonstrations now retain the complete orbit in the camera frame at every slider angle.
releases.developers: Removed a competing CSS override and obsolete JavaScript card-toggle behavior, replaced nonsemantic whole-card click targets with native HTML disclosures, converted eight planet controls to buttons with aria-pressed, and added a 28-page UI structural regression gate. Verified against actual mobile and desktop browsers. Follow-up dfbeea2 synchronizes Moon Phases 0/90/180/270° preset aria-pressed with the slider and both Spring/Neap selected states without changing scientific calculations. Follow-up 593010b adds static-first HTML values, disabled-until-ready controls and ci/verify_ready_content.mjs to both Pages deployment and scheduled site health; production and blocked-JavaScript browser flows verified. Follow-up b2ee470 fixes OrbitControls silently clamping the camera inside the lunar orbit, adds aspect-aware camera fitting on resize and 360-degree orbital-frustum regression coverage for eight viewport shapes.

releases.title: A clearer search button on small screens
releases.summary: The search control now lives beside the Space Atlas logo instead of interrupting the horizontally scrolling topic links. The second navigation row is smaller and dedicated to browsing lessons.
releases.students: Tap the magnifying-glass icon at the top right to search. The row below now contains only lesson navigation links, including All topics.
releases.teachers: The full topic directory and direct lesson links remain available from mobile. The search dialog and keyboard focus return work as before without covering or rearranging the study material.
releases.developers: Following Android screenshot review, separated the utility-owned 42px SVG search trigger from the 44px-high mobile link strip, removed conflicting narrow-screen CSS overrides and emoji icon, preserved search dialog IDs and accessibility, and added a 28-page mobile-header CI gate with 320/390/768/980/1024px+ browser verification.

releases.title: Move from one space question to the next
releases.summary: Topic breadcrumbs now lead to real category sections, mobile readers can find the full atlas directory and search immediately, and related lesson cards recommend distinct next questions instead of repeating the same destination.
releases.students: From any lesson, use the linked topic breadcrumb to return to its subject directory, or choose an evidence-based next question in Keep exploring.
releases.teachers: Guide learners between models, measured facts and adjacent concepts using explicit category and recommended-lesson links; the science citations and model limitations remain unchanged.
releases.developers: Repaired eight duplicated Go deeper targets, linked all 26 category breadcrumbs to four real homepage anchors, and exposed the topic directory and search earlier on mobile. Added a deterministic 28-page user-flow graph, canonical/sitemap and fragment validation gate; existing JSON-LD avoids invented indexable category hubs.

releases.title: Find related lessons and sources more easily
releases.summary: The shared footer has been reorganized so its science explanation, learning pathways, project resources and release history stay aligned and readable on phones and larger screens.
releases.students: Follow the Solar System, Earth & Moon, and Deep Space links from the bottom of any lesson without hunting through a dense block of notes.
releases.teachers: Model limitations, primary learning sources and project updates are now directly accessible from a labelled and keyboard-navigable footer.
releases.developers: Replaced an unstructured one-line footer and a grid placement rule on a non-grid child with one semantic component. Added a 28-page shared-footer hierarchy and route regression gate, alongside 320/390/1280px browser checks.

releases.title: Search and motion controls respond to your choices
releases.summary: Keyboard search now closes without unexpected navigation; the solar-system model respects reduced-motion preferences, and shared quizzes provide assistive-technology feedback.
releases.students: Search topics with a keyboard and follow your intended selection. Motion-sensitive visitors start with a still 3D solar-system scene and may choose to resume it.
releases.teachers: Keyboard navigation, a reduced-motion default and quiz status announcements make common classroom interactions more predictable. Screen-reader behavior still benefits from device-specific testing.
releases.developers: Resolved global Enter interception, late search-index loading, hidden-tab WebGL frame scheduling, and live-region semantics. Added a dedicated browser-flow/DOM regression gate and a prioritized code-quality audit.

releases.title: Understand why outer planets have longer years
releases.summary: A Kepler’s-law explorer links each planet’s orbit size with its orbital period. Behind the scenes, scheduled checks now test the published site.
releases.students: Choose a planet to compare its year with an idealized orbital-period prediction.
releases.teachers: Use the log-scale chart to introduce Kepler’s third law; check the stated model limitations before classroom use.
releases.developers: Introduced opt-in release-safe automated site health checks and added a Kepler model regression gate.

releases.title: Explore temperature, tides and honest distance scales
releases.summary: New controls reveal signed planetary temperatures, changing lunar–solar alignment, and differences between physical AU distances and compressed model coordinates.
releases.students: Compare two planets’ temperatures, vary the Moon’s alignment, or follow a planet across two distance rulers.
releases.teachers: Read surface-vs-atmosphere temperature caveats and explain why the tide-force diagram is not a local tide forecast.
releases.developers: Added source-based interaction tests, explicit units and static evidence tables.

releases.title: Find our place in the Milky Way and apply the planet rule
releases.summary: New galaxy-viewing, Milky Way distance and dwarf-planet classification tools replace passive descriptions with testable choices.
releases.students: Move a viewpoint or ruler and compare Pluto with other Solar System bodies.
releases.teachers: Use the distinction between observed evidence, geometric illustrations and the IAU definition as a discussion prompt.
releases.developers: Kept original explanatory text and citations accessible without JavaScript.

releases.title: Planet sizes now use one scale; real images inform 3D views
releases.summary: Corrected the Earth–Moon center separation and planet diameter comparisons, and added optional sourced 3D exterior views.
releases.students: See honest planetary size ratios, change Earth–Moon distance and rotate planet views.
releases.teachers: Compare measured planetary dimensions with conceptual views; Neptune’s texture is clearly labeled as an illustration.
releases.developers: Uses on-demand Three.js views and shared physical scales without altering existing indexed routes.

releases.title: Read telescope imagery, spectrum and stellar paths
releases.summary: New evidence-led comparisons help distinguish what telescopes observe from models, illustrations and inferred science.
releases.students: Compare Hubble and Webb views, explore light beyond visible colors, and follow alternative stellar evolution paths.
releases.teachers: Use image attribution, wavelength labels and model limitations as teaching references.
releases.developers: Original NASA imagery is credited and optimized; scientific uncertainties remain explicit in the static page.

releases.title: Classroom exploration and sharing improvements
releases.summary: A small teacher-oriented distribution experiment added classroom context to three selected astronomy lessons.
releases.students: Continue using the same science models; the learning content remains available.
releases.teachers: Selected lessons include classroom-use prompts and sharing actions; this is an experiment, not a claimed measured learning result.
releases.developers: Experiment is scoped to three established lessons instead of added across the full site.
